body.p: Claims 1-10 are pending in the application. Reconsideration of the objection and rejections set forth in the aforementioned Office Action is respectfully requested in view of the above amended claims and following remarks. The basis for these amended claims can be found throughout the specification, claims and drawings as originally filed.

Applicant respectfully submits that the above amended claims overcome the current objection and rejections of record and, as such, all the claims are now in condition for allowance. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests completion of prosecution and issuance of a Notice of Allowance. However, should the Examiner elect to issue an Office Action in response to this Amendment, Applicant hereby requests a telephonic interview with the Examiner prior to issuance of any Office Action in order to discuss any remaining issues.

Applicant respectfully acknowledges the Examiner's interpretation of Claims 4, 5, 7 and 8 in the Office Action. However, Applicant respectfully submits that the Examiner's interpretation in this regard may too narrowly define Applicant's noted claim terms and that Applicant's noted claim terms could be characterized more broadly. As such, Applicant does not acquiesce that the noted claim terms are to be interpreted as solely, exactly expressed by the Examiner.

Claim 8 stands objected to because of various "informalities." Pursuant to the Examiner's suggestion and recommendation, a minor amendment to Claim 8 has been made in order to address the noted informality. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner to reconsider and withdraw the objection to Claim 8.

Claims 1-8 and 10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Poeppel et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2023/0205202 in view of Wilson et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2019/0361451. Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.

Additionally/alternatively, Claims 4, 5 and 7 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Poeppel et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2023/0205202 in view of Wilson et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2019/0361451 and further in view of Yasuda et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2019/0278278. Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.

Claim 9 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Poeppel et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2023/0205202 in view of Wilson et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2019/0361451 and further in view of Christen et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2019/0219411. Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.
Applicant respectfully disagrees with the Examiner's characterization that Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any

of the other references cited, renders Applicant's claimed disclosure obvious. Additionally, there is no motivation or incentive in Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited, to arrive at Applicant's disclosure as claimed. It is respectfully submitted that Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited, teaches away from Applicant's unique and innovative vehicle control system and vehicle control device. Applicant's claimed disclosure recites an improved vehicle control system and vehicle control device having a unique and advantageous orientation and combination of components which are more efficient, advantageous, and eliminate various negative features associated with the devices/systems disclosed in the cited references.

Applicant's claimed disclosure is directed toward an improved vehicle control system and vehicle control device which are capable of maintaining safety and appropriately providing relief to a failed autonomous driving vehicle. Applicant's improved vehicle control system and vehicle control device are able to accomplish these tasks as a result of their unique and advantageous arrangement and orientation of components and features.

First, amended independent Claims 1 and 6 of Applicant's claimed disclosure recite: "recognize, based on information indicating fault of a device used for autonomous driving or information indicating temporarily unusable state of the device which are transmitted from the vehicle control device, that the autonomous driving vehicle terminates autonomous driving."
Poeppel et al. describes "a user may transmit a text message, or other electronic message" in paragraph [0030].

It should be noted that in this application, a determination of termination of autonomous driving is performed without a driver or a passenger. In order to clarify/distinguish this aspect, the feature "based on information indicating fault of a device used for autonomous driving or information indicating temporarily unusable state of the device which are transmitted from the vehicle control device" has been added.
Second, regarding a second stop position, amended independent Claims 1 and 6 of Applicant's claimed disclosure recite:

"[the vehicle control device...configured to] set a second stop position for stopping the autonomous driving vehicle, the second stop position being a nearest position to a present position of the autonomous driving vehicle, which is selected from predetermined positions"; and

"[the vehicle control device...configured to] initiate travel of the autonomous driving vehicle toward the second stop position without waiting for receiving of the first stop position transmitted from the center device, upon setting the second stop position."

Wilson et al. discloses a rendezvous location. According to Wilson et al., "a rendezvous location is determined in step 332, and an arrival time is determined in step 336 at which the emergency medical vehicle and the autonomous automotive vehicle are estimated to simultaneously arrive at the rendezvous location."

It should be noted that EMS information is required in order to decide "the rendezvous location." In other words, it is impossible to decide the rendezvous location only by information in an autonomous automotive vehicle.
There is a difference between the "second stop position" recited in amended independent Claims 1 and 6 of Applicant's claimed disclosure and the "rendezvous location" of Wilson et al.

In order to clarify/distinguish a relationship between the first stop position and the second stop position, the feature "initiate travel of the autonomous driving vehicle toward the second stop position without waiting for receiving of the first stop position transmitted from the center device, upon setting the second stop position" has been added.

Applicant's first stop position is set by a center device, which is located outside the vehicle. Applicant's second stop position is set by a vehicle control device. As described in Applicant's specification, even when the first stop position cannot be obtained, the vehicle control device can cause the vehicle to stop at the second stop position. That is, steps S150, S160, S180 and S190 in FIG. 2 of Applicant's application describe that when the second stop position is set, the vehicle starts travelling without reception of a first stop position.

Finally, amended independent Claims 1 and 6 of Applicant's claimed disclosure recite: "the first stop position is decided by the center device and the second stop position is decided by the vehicle control device."

Poeppel et al. describes "[i]n response, the autonomous vehicle can initiate a motion plan that can include a trajectory to and a controlled stop at a destination representing a safe state" in paragraph [0037]. However, Poeppel et al. does not disclose, teach or suggest "a destination" decided by a remote computing system.

As such, Poeppel et al. does not disclose, teach or suggest "the first stop position is decided by the center device" as recited in amended independent Claims 1 and 6 of Applicant's claimed disclosure.

Wilson et al. discloses "a rendezvous location", "a rendezvous location is determined in step 332", and "it is implemented by a computer system within the autonomous automotive vehicle which includes wireless communication capabilities."

According to amended independent Claims 1 and 6 of Applicant's claimed disclosure, the autonomous driving vehicle has a second stop position when terminating the autonomous driving. And when the autonomous driving vehicle has both a second stop position and a first stop position, the autonomous driving vehicle goes to the first stop position.
Even when Poeppel et al. and Wilson et al. are combined, a priority of the first and second stop positions is not disclosed, taught or suggested.

Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited, does not disclose, teach or suggest any structure similar to Applicant's vehicle control system and vehicle control device as recited in amended independent Claims 1 and 6 of Applicant's claimed disclosure. There is no motivation or incentive in Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited, to arrive at Applicant's disclosure as claimed. In fact, the cited references teach away from and articulate various disadvantages associated with the arrangement, configuration and orientation of components taught in Applicant's claimed disclosure.

Thus, Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited, does not disclose, teach or suggest Applicant's unique and innovative vehicle control system and vehicle control device as recited in amended independent Claims 1 and 6 of Applicant's claimed disclosure. The deficiencies found in Poeppel et al. are not corrected by the combination of Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited. Additionally, there is no motivation or incentive in Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited, to arrive at Applicant's disclosure as claimed. Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that amended independent Claims 1 and 6, and all claims depending directly or indirectly therefrom (Claims 2-5 and 7-10), are not obvious in light of and are patentable over Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited.

Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that in view of Applicant's succinct arguments set forth above and previously, Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited, fails to disclose, teach or suggest several features that are recited in Applicant's claimed disclosure. As such, Applicant's unique and innovative vehicle control system and vehicle control device are not disclosed, taught or suggested by Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited.
Without conceding to the correctness of the Examiner's comments thereto, Applicant respectfully submits that Claims 2-5 and 7-10 are allowable, at least, for the
same reasons given above for amended independent Claims 1 and 6, because Claims 2-5 and 7-10 are ultimately dependent on either amended independent Claim 1 or amended independent Claim 6.

It is respectfully submitted that in view of Applicant's arguments stated above and previously, Poeppel et al. is an improper primary reference, Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. are improper secondary references, and Applicant's claims are patentably distinct with respect thereto, as well as no teaching in existence to suggest the combination of any of the cited references. As set forth in MPEP § 2142, "the key to supporting any rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 103 is the clear articulation of the reason(s) why the claimed invention would have been obvious." As the U.S. Supreme Court noted in KSR Intl. Co. v. Teleflex Inc., "the analysis supporting a rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 103 should be made explicit." 82 USPQ2d 1385, 1396 (2007). The Federal Circuit has stated that "rejections on obviousness cannot be sustained by mere conclusory statements; instead, there must be some articulated reasoning with some rational underpinning to support the legal conclusion of obviousness." In re Kahn, 441 F.3d 977 at 988, 78 USPQ2d 1329 at 1336 (Fed. Cir. 2006). In the Office Action, the Examiner's conclusory statements are insufficient to establish a prima facie rejection because no articulated reasoning with rational underpinning was given, and no explanation as to exactly how the combination or modification could have been made was provided. As a result, Applicant respectfully submits that the Examiner has failed to identify any motivation by one of ordinary skill in the art to combine or modify the art to arrive at the claimed disclosure other than the impermissible use of hindsight.

While it is Applicant's view that the claims as written are not obvious in light of the cited art and fully comply with Section 103, in the interest of advancing and expediting prosecution, and without prejudice to pursuing this and related subject matter in future applications, Applicant has amended independent Claims 1 and 6. Therefore, amended independent Claims 1 and 6 should be in condition for allowance. Further, because Claims 2-5 and 7-10 depend from either amended independent Claim 1 or amended independent Claim 6, directly or indirectly, they are at least as limited, are similarly not taught by Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited, and should also be in condition for allowance. In view of the above amendments and these remarks, Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner to reconsider and withdraw the Section 103 rejections to Claims 1-10.

All of the stated grounds of objection and rejection have been properly traversed, accommodated or rendered moot. Applicant therefore respectfully requests the Examiner to reconsider all presently outstanding objections and rejections and that they be withdrawn. It is believed that a full and complete response has been made to the outstanding Office Action and, as such, the present application is in condition for allowance. Thus, prompt and favorable consideration of this Amendment is respectfully requested. If the Examiner believes that personal communication will expedite prosecution of this application, they are invited to contact the undersigned at their earliest convenience.
Dated: June 24, 2024 Respectfully submitted,
